main_issue: Whether alcohol should be served at the Saturday housewarming in the shared flat, given D's religious objection to hosting it, versus A and B's wish to serve it to guests.

A-B.evidence: B backs A's cooler-box compromise (14) and agrees A has a point against moving to a bar (24); both keep wanting drinks for guests.

A-C.evidence: C questions A's cooler compromise (15) and proposes no-alcohol/bar plans, which A rejects (23); C concedes A's point on the awkward bar move (25), but the time split is also unresolved (27).

A-D.evidence: A: 'a lot of our guests drink' (11); D: 'I can't be a host at a party where alcohol is served' (12); D rejects the cooler idea (16); no one shifts.

B-C.evidence: B calls the cooler a fair compromise (14) while C doubts it (15); B objects to the bar plan (24); C concedes it is awkward (25) but still sides with D's concern.

B-D.evidence: B supports the cooler compromise (14) which D says doesn't solve it (16); B objects to the no-alcohol bar split D accepted (24).

C-D.evidence: C asks about D's concerns (5, 15) and proposes the bar split which D accepts (20-21); C agrees the time split doesn't fix it for D (27); D thanks C (28).
